OneDrive: your app at Microsoft

Once, on a computer: entra.microsoft.com › App registrations › New registration. For account types, pick the one that includes personal Microsoft accounts. Then, under Authentication, turn on “Allow public client flows”. Copy the “Application (client) ID” and type it here (you can type from your phone, in the panel).
Application (client) ID
On your phone or computer, open microsoft.com/link (or point the camera at the QR) and type the code below. The TV only asks to read files.
Microsoft did not accept this app. Check the ID and that “Allow public client flows” is on.

Once, on a computer: dropbox.com/developers/apps › Create app › Scoped access › Full Dropbox. In the Permissions tab, tick files.metadata.read, files.content.read and account_info.read and save (Submit). Copy the “App key” and type it here.
App key
The App key has only lowercase letters and numbers.
Point your phone camera at the QR, sign in to Dropbox and tap Allow. Dropbox shows a code: type it here (you can type from your phone, in the panel).
Dropbox code
Type the whole code Dropbox showed.

Once, on a computer: app.box.com/developers/console › Create New App › Custom App › User Authentication (OAuth 2.0). In the Configuration tab, under OAuth 2.0 Redirect URI, put %1$s and leave only “Read all files and folders” ticked. Save, then copy the Client ID and the Client Secret here.
Client ID
Client Secret
Client ID and Client Secret have only letters and numbers. Copy both from the Configuration tab.
The TV is not on the home network. Connect it and try again.
Point the camera of a phone that is on the same Wi‑Fi as the TV at the QR, sign in to %1$s and allow access. The phone comes back to the TV by itself: nothing to type.
Port %1$d on the TV is busy. Close other apps and try again.

Once, on a computer, in your Google Cloud project (console.cloud.google.com): APIs & Services › Library › turn on “Google Drive API”. In Google Auth Platform › Data Access, add the …/auth/drive.readonly scope. In Clients › Create client › Web application, under Authorized redirect URIs put %1$s. Copy the Client ID and the Client secret here.
Client ID (…apps.googleusercontent.com)
Client secret
Copy both from the client page: the ID ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com and the secret usually starts with GOCSPX-.
If Google says the app is not verified, tap Advanced › Go to (it is your own app).
